findings.source_text: kept them under no severer discipline than what was absolutely best for them, and had been less kindness to have slackened

findings.suggested_fix: keeping them under no severer discipline than was absolutely best for them — discipline that it would have been less kind to relax.

findings.source_text: And so lunatics and ideots are never set free from the government of their parents;

findings.source_text: children, who are not as yet come unto those years whereat they may have; and innocents which are excluded by a natural defect from ever having
findings.candidate_text: “Children, who have not yet come to those years at which they may have it; and innocents, who are excluded by a natural defect from ever having it

findings.suggested_fix: “Children, who have not yet come to those years at which they may have the use of reason; and innocents, who are excluded by a natural defect from ever having it; …

findings.source_text: yet when time, giving authority, and (as some men would persuade us) sacredness of customs, which the negligent, and unforeseeing innocence of the first ages began, had brought in successors of another stamp
findings.candidate_text: Yet in time — which gave authority and (as some men would persuade us) sacredness to customs that the careless and unforeseeing innocence of the first ages had begun — successors of another kind came in.
findings.problem: Renderer-flagged (their index 20 = 0-based 19): the reading 'time giving authority and sacredness to customs' is right, but 'successors … came in' drops Locke's causal agency: time and hallowed custom brought those successors in (as the hereditary succession of custom), which is the point of the sentence.
findings.suggested_fix: Yet when time — giving authority and (as some men would persuade us) sacredness to customs that the careless and unforeseeing innocence of the first ages had begun — had brought in successors of another kind, the people found …

summary: I compared every paragraph of chapters 6 (27) and 7 (22) with the source, including all 17 sampled paragraphs and all 6 renderer-flagged ones. The renderer's flagged indices are 1-based: ch6 '17' is 0-based 16, ch6 '2' is 1, ch6 '9–10' is 8–9, and ch7 '20' is 19; this file uses 0-based indices. I found no major fidelity problems. Terms are stable (state of nature, legislative, property, consent, commonwealth, executive power of the law of nature), and the Hooker notes are modernized, complete, quoted, and cited as 'Hooker, Ecclesiastical Polity, book I, section N' with the (* and (** markers kept. Scripture is left in KJV wording. The must-fix is the ungrammatical 'and than it would have been less kind to relax' (ch6 p16). The other fixes are small: dropped connectives and qualifiers ('only', 'all', 'And therefore'), the lost causal agency of 'time … had brought in successors' (ch7 p19), and the dangling 'it' at the start of the ch6 p9 Hooker quotation. A whole-chapter grep found no term drift and no residual archaisms: every 'possession(s)' matches Locke's own word, and 'legislature' at ch7 p19 is Locke's.
